label: Japanese romcom light novel
description: School-year romantic comedy: a witty first-person narrator, forced proximity, misunderstandings and a confession earned over festivals and exams.
voice: First person, past tense, a witty and self-deprecating narrator who notices everything except what matters most.
Banter-heavy dialogue with clear voices; honorifics (-san, -kun, -senpai) signal distance and change when feelings change.
The school calendar gives the book its rhythm: seating changes, exams, summer break, the culture festival, the first snow.
Comedy from character, not slapstick: pride, misunderstanding, stubbornness.
Small gestures carry the romance: a shared umbrella, a lunch box, a message left on read.
End chapters on a line that makes the reader want the next scene between them.

structure.guide: A memorable meeting that sets up their dynamic and a reason they cannot avoid each other.
Circumstances bind them: neighbours, a club, a fake relationship, a tutoring deal.
structure.then: Daily scenes that build trust; each chapter reveals one new side of the love interest.

structure.guide: An outing that is definitely not a date, which goes wrong and right.
A rival or a past connection appears and exposes the narrator's feelings to himself.
The narrator admits, privately, what he feels, and panics.
structure.then: He tries and fails to act normal; she notices.

structure.guide: A misunderstanding or a family problem pushes them apart.
A big school event where everything comes to a head in public.
The confession, in their own awkward, specific way.
A short scene of the new normal with one teasing line.

outline_guidance: Each chapter has a concrete situation (a test, a shared chore, an outing) and moves the relationship by one visible step, forward or back.
outline_example: Umbrella Rules | When the rain traps them at Minami Station, Takeda Ren shares his umbrella with Shiina Yui and sets absurd rules about the distance | She follows the rules so literally that he has to admit he wants her closer | Yui's older sister sees them from a bus window
scene_guidance: Open on the situation, not on the weather.
Keep misunderstandings short; the reader should never feel the characters are stupid.
Let friends comment like a chorus.
worldbuilding: The school, the class, the club, the neighbourhood.
Each lead's home life and one private worry.
naming: Japanese names, family name first in narration of formal settings (Takeda Ren, Shiina Yui); given names only once they are close.
cliches: tripped and fell on top of
sample:
"Rule three," I said. "The umbrella belongs to whoever is taller."

"That's you."

"Which is why it's a good rule."

Shiina-san looked at the rain, then at the ten centimetres of dry air between our shoulders, as if measuring it for a report.

"And rule four?"

I didn't have a rule four. I made one up. It was a mistake.
